title: World-VLA-Loop: Closed-Loop Learning of Video World Model and VLA Policy
why: Exact collision candidate: policy failure rollouts iteratively refine the video world model, which then supplies virtual RL rollouts for the VLA; the proposal must show why an independently held reality anchor prevents a failure this co-evolving loop does not address.

title: VLAW: Iterative Co-Improvement of Vision-Language-Action Policy and World Model
why: Direct iterative VLA-world-model co-training neighbor: real policy rollouts improve world-model fidelity and generated rollouts improve the policy, making it load-bearing for separating the proposed cross-fitted reality interface from naive alternation.

title: WoVR: World Models as Reliable Simulators for Post-Training VLA Policies with RL
why: Explicitly targets hallucination-driven policy exploitation and maintains policy-simulator alignment through world-model-policy co-evolution; it is the closest baseline for proving that anchor separation adds more than rollout stabilization or uncertainty control.

title: Feedback World Model Enables Precise Guidance of Diffusion Policy
why: Uses real post-action prediction residuals as an online feedback state to correct a world model under distribution shift, closely neighboring the reality-anchor intuition while remaining inference-time feedback rather than cross-fitted co-training.

title: World-Gymnast: Training Robots with Reinforcement Learning in a World Model
why: Trains a VLA by imagined rollouts with VLM rewards and reports online iterative world-model and policy improvement; it is a direct comparator for shared-evaluator self-confirmation and for the value of an external reality anchor.

title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning
why: Newest diagnostic of the exact off-expert regime where imagined-policy optimization is vulnerable: it shows action-conditioned world models can ignore commanded actions or generate invalid rollouts and proposes intervention-effect alignment, a crucial competing explanation and baseline.

title: Imperfect World Models are Exploitable
why: Formalizes model exploitation as policy-order inversion and shows low predictive error need not prevent it, providing the theory-level justification for why generic validation or prediction accuracy cannot rule out self-confirming shared errors.

title: Cross-fitted Proximal Learning for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
why: Recent explicit K-fold cross-fitting ancestor in model-based RL; although aimed at bridge estimation under hidden confounding rather than VLA-WAM co-adaptation, it is load-bearing prior art for any claimed novelty in a cross-fitted interface.
